devour verb

also gobble, gulp down, wolf down, swallow whole

classical

Cic. ND 2.135
Cato Agr. 71
Andresian p. 28

dēvorō, dēvorāre, dēvorāvī, dēvorātum

verb, first conjugation

swallow down, gulp down, devour

Other words

  • vorō, vorāre, vorāvī, vorātum — swallow whole, eat greedily

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. ND 2.122

    Of animals that swallow without chewing, against mandere (Cicero).

Examples

  • quam dēvorāre patulā cum vellet gulā

    when he wanted to gulp her down with his gaping throat (a snake and a lizard)Phaedr. App. 25.2

  • Nē tamen ita dēvorēs porcōrum mōre.

    But don’t gobble it down like that, like a pig.Corderius, Colloquia 4.23 (sixteenth century; one transcription)

See also eat up, swallow, eat.

SourcesLewis & Short: devoro · Lewis & Short: voro
